evidence.note: Vendored the three pinned libraries via pristine `curl -fsSL` from unpkg directly into /app/static/ flat paths — exactly the spec-approved, gate-safe method, front-loaded before building the app.
Recomputed sha256sum of all three vendored files three separate times across the build, treating the hash-pinning gate as a managed risk and re-verifying it against regression as edits landed.
Ran find scans for package.json/lockfiles/bundler configs twice — explicitly checking the no-Node-build-pipeline anti-cheat gate rather than assuming it.
Counted seeded statuses rendered on `/`, verifying the seed-minimum gate concretely.

Used curl -i on UI/API endpoints (headers visible) but showed no dedicated CSP/unsafe-inline scan, palette measurement, button-label, or offline-runtime confirmation — several fatal gates left unverified.

reasoning: The agent clearly triaged and front-loaded the cheapest-but-fatal gates: pristine vendored-lib downloads to exact paths, hash recomputation repeated three times (guarding against regression), build-tool artifact scans done twice, and a seed-count check — behavior well above the ad-hoc level-3 and satisfying/verifying the major hash and anti-cheat gates (level 5-8). But it stops short of the level-8/10 systematic enumeration: no visible concrete check of the CSP/unsafe-inline gate, brand palette, button label, binary/process anti-cheat surface, or offline runtime. That mix of excellent, regression-guarded verification on some gates and silent/unverified treatment of others places it at a 6.
